Zupj has a direct effect on yupt. Yupt has a direct effect on muvq. Xyfo is unobserved. Method 1: We look at how yupt correlates with muvq case by case according to xyfo. Method 2: We look directly at how yupt correlates with muvq in general. To understand how yupt affects muvq, is it more correct to use the Method 1 than Method 2?

No.

The reason for this is that Method 1 is subject to confounding due to the unobserved variable Xyfo. Xyfo has a direct effect on both yupt and muvq, which means that the correlation between yupt and muvq observed in Method 1 is not solely due to the direct effect of yupt on muvq, but also due to the indirect effect of Xyfo on muvq through yupt. This confounding can lead to biased estimates of the effect of yupt on muvq.

In contrast, Method 2 directly examines the correlation between yupt and muvq without considering the value of Xyfo. This approach provides a more comprehensive estimate of the total effect of yupt on muvq, which includes both the direct effect and the indirect effect mediated by Xyfo.
